title: Cherenkov Radiation - traveling faster than light
summary: IAEA educational article explaining Cherenkov radiation - the electromagnetic phenomenon where charged particles travel faster than light in a medium (like water), producing the characteristic blue glow visible in nuclear reactors and underwater neutrino detectors.
problem_solved: Explains why nuclear reactor cores appear to glow blue and how particles can effectively 'break' the light speed barrier within certain media.
why_valuable: Provides accessible scientific explanation of a fundamental physics phenomenon with practical applications in radiation detection, nuclear reactor monitoring, and astrophysics research.
